images.text: Friend: You're really the best at what you do, Mark. You're number one every month in your job and this one you're taking the lead too. That's impressive. How do you do it?
Sales rep: I guess it is the experience. Two days ago, for example, I was making a presentation to sell the company's new information system and everything went really well.
Friend: Excuse my ignorance, Mark, but what's an information system, a computer software?

Sales rep: Not exactly, it's much more than that. In simple terms, it is a compilation of integrated components that are used to collect, store, retrieve and distribute data, knowledge and information within a company, from and to its external stakeholders, and to those who need it for the purpose of planning, making decisions, coordinating processes and controlling activities and results.
Friend: Wow! It's a long definition. Do you usually study it?
Sales rep: Not at all. As I said before, it's the product of experience.
Friend: I see. Tell me more, Mark. You weren't giving all this information to your clients when you made the presentation, were you?

Sales rep: Of course. In fact, at this time that day, they were asking me lots of questions about it. After the definition, I told them about the components of an IS.
Friend: And what are they?

Sales rep: Well, it basically includes the hardware, software, communications infrastructure, trained personnel and users' experience. With all of them together, function and structure are guaranteed. Managers and workers can complete important tasks like analyzing problems, visualizing complex subjects, and creating new products thanks to modeling programs.
Friend: You mention users, why are they important for an IS?
Sales rep: Because all the enormous effort is conducive to satisfy users' everyday needs. That's what counts!

Past Continuous in Affirmative and Negative
The Past Continuous Tense has several uses, but generally speaking, it refers to actions that were happening for some time in the past.
I was making a presentation to sell the company's new information system and everything went really well.
You weren't giving all this information to your clients when you made the presentation, were you?

The Past Continuous Tense can be used in affirmative, negative and interrogative forms. It refers to actions in a specific time in past, an action before another important action or two actions at the same time.

Notice that when there are two actions happening at the same time, you can use “while or as”.

Example:
- I was checking my files while/as the engineers were updating the net.
Simple Past and Simple Present with Time Expressions
Either tense, Simple Past or Simple Present is connected to time expressions that help clarify when the action takes place.
You weren't giving all this information to your clients when you made the presentation, were you?
You're number one every month in your job and this one you're taking the lead too.
Do you usually study?

Simple Past is used to express the idea that an action already finished at a specific time in the past.
Remember, use simple past to state the action was over and not in progress.

There are many time expressions associated to Simple Past. Let's take a look at some of them as they are said in English:

- Yesterday, yesterday morning/evening/afternoon, etc.
- The day before yesterday, the night before last night, etc.
- Last night, last week, last year, last month, last time, etc.
- This afternoon, this evening, that morning, that day, etc.
- An hour ago, a month ago, three years ago, minutes ago, a long time ago, etc.
- In 1999, in March, in March last year, in my 20s, in the 20s, etc.
- On Sunday, on 7th October 1956, on my birthday, etc.
- When I was at school, when I was younger, when she came home, etc.

Examples:
- I had an appointment with one of our clients last week, but he could not attend us that day as his mother died the day before.

Simple Present  is used to state facts, generalizations, scheduled events and routines. 

As with the Simple Past, there are many  time expressions  associated to Simple Present. Some of them are described as follows:

- Always, usually, often, regularly, generally, rarely, never, etc.
- Once a day, twice a week, three times a month, every day, etc.
- On Fridays, on Mondays, at the weekends, in the week, etc.
- In the afternoon, in the afternoons, in the evening, etc.
- In winter, in spring, in autumn, in summer
- Weekly, monthly, daily, annually, etc.
- Every summer, every holiday, every season, etc.
- At 6 o'clock, at night, at noon, etc. 

Example:
- I check my e-mail twice a day , once  in the morning  and other  in the afternoon .
